title: Mealworms to Beetles: Parent Guide
endLine: A mealworm becomes a pupa, then an adult beetle.

scenes.tts: Is a mealworm a worm? It looks like one. But keep a few in a tub for some weeks, and something else climbs out.
scenes.caption: Is a mealworm a worm? It looks like one. But keep a few in a tub for some weeks, and something else climbs out.
scenes.visual: Warm schematic close-up of a clear plastic tub of oats filling most of the frame. A few pale yellow-tan mealworms wriggle slowly over a thin carrot slice. Large high-contrast text: 'A worm?' A faint beetle silhouette waits at the edge of frame. No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: Is a mealworm a worm? It looks like one. But keep a few in a tub for some weeks, and something else climbs out.

scenes.visual: Same tub. The title 'Mealworms to Beetles' appears above the lid while the mealworms keep moving slowly.

scenes.tts: A kitten looks like a small cat from birth. A mealworm changes into a beetle. At each visit, your child counts and records what they see. Over time, they can check what changed.
scenes.caption: A kitten looks like a small cat from birth. A mealworm changes into a beetle. At each visit, your child counts and records what they see. Over time, they can check what changed.
scenes.visual: Split frame: left, a drawn kitten beside a grown cat, with a matching arrow; right, a mealworm beside a dark beetle, with a question mark on the arrow. Then three short labels appear by the tub: 'Count', 'Record', 'Wait and check'.
scenes.narration: A kitten looks like a small cat from birth. A mealworm changes into a beetle. At each visit, your child counts and records what they see. Over time, they can check what changed.

scenes.tts: You need ten to twenty ordinary mealworms from a bait shop or pet store, not giant ones. Add a clear plastic tub with a lid, rolled oats or wheat bran, and a carrot or potato.
scenes.caption: You need ten to twenty ordinary mealworms from a bait shop or pet store, not giant ones. Add a clear plastic tub with a lid, rolled oats or wheat bran, and a carrot or potato.
scenes.visual: Friendly drawn objects settle around the tub, at most six: a small carton of mealworms, the clear tub and lid, a bag of oats, a carrot, a plastic spoon and a soft paintbrush. Each has a two- or three-word label.
scenes.narration: You need ten to twenty ordinary mealworms from a bait shop or pet store, not giant ones. Add a clear plastic tub with a lid, rolled oats or wheat bran, and a carrot or potato.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child whenever the tub is open. Keep the lid on between visits. Keep insects, bedding, and vegetable slices away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep everything out of mouths. Wash hands with soap after each visit.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child whenever the tub is open. Keep the lid on between visits. Keep insects, bedding, and vegetable slices away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep everything out of mouths. Wash hands with soap after each visit.
scenes.visual: Show an adult beside the open tub. Then show the closed clear tub on a high shelf, with the insects, bedding, and carrot slices visible inside it. Label the contents “Under 4: choking risk.” Show a phone labeled “Choking? Call 911” and finish with soapy hands.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child whenever the tub is open. Keep the lid on between visits. Keep insects, bedding, and vegetable slices away from children under four. Call nine one one if a child is choking. Keep everything out of mouths. Wash hands with soap after each visit.

scenes.tts: If your child has asthma or a shellfish or dust mite allergy, ask their doctor first. For wheat allergy, use only bedding their allergist approves. Skip if in doubt. Open the tub away from faces. If breathing is hard, call nine one one.
scenes.caption: If your child has asthma or a shellfish or dust mite allergy, ask their doctor first. For wheat allergy, use only bedding their allergist approves. Skip if in doubt. Open the tub away from faces. If breathing is hard, call nine one one.
scenes.visual: Keep the tub in frame. Show an adult holding the lid away from faces, with the oats and bran beside the tub. Use short labels for checking with the doctor and for the bedding allergy check. End on a phone icon labeled “Breathing hard? Call 911.”
scenes.narration: If your child has asthma or a shellfish or dust mite allergy, ask their doctor first. For wheat allergy, use only bedding their allergist approves. Skip if in doubt. Open the tub away from faces. If breathing is hard, call nine one one.

scenes.tts: With the lid flat, poke ten to twenty small air holes. Add oats or bran three to five centimeters deep. Cut two thin carrot slices and lay them on top. They provide water.
scenes.caption: With the lid flat, poke ten to twenty small air holes. Add oats or bran three to five centimeters deep. Cut two thin carrot slices and lay them on top. They provide water.
scenes.visual: An adult hand pokes holes in a lid lying flat on a table with a skewer. The tub fills with an oat layer; a bracket marks '3 to 5 cm'. Two thin carrot slices settle on top, with a small water-drop icon beside them.
scenes.narration: With the lid flat, poke ten to twenty small air holes. Add oats or bran three to five centimeters deep. Cut two thin carrot slices and lay them on top. They provide water.

scenes.tts: Tip the mealworms onto a plate. Use a hand lens to count legs together. Ask, 'What do you think it will turn into?' Record the guess. Measure two or three mealworms. Then spoon all the mealworms into the tub.
scenes.caption: Tip the mealworms onto a plate. Use a hand lens to count legs together. Ask, 'What do you think it will turn into?' Record the guess. Measure two or three mealworms. Then spoon all the mealworms into the tub.
scenes.visual: Show six small legs near a mealworm’s head under a hand lens. Hold on the paper plate as a notepad marked “Our guess” and a metric ruler slide into view. Show the adult using a plastic spoon to move the mealworms into the prepared tub.
scenes.narration: Tip the mealworms onto a plate. Use a hand lens to count legs together. Ask, 'What do you think it will turn into?' Record the guess. Measure two or three mealworms. Then spoon all the mealworms into the tub.

scenes.tts: Keep the tub at room temperature and out of direct sun. Visit two or three times a week. Look for shed skins. Count and record each stage. Replace the carrot every two or three days.
scenes.caption: Keep the tub at room temperature and out of direct sun. Visit two or three times a week. Look for shed skins. Count and record each stage. Replace the carrot every two or three days.
scenes.visual: The tub sits on a shelf away from a sunny window. A simple calendar strip advances with check marks two or three times a week. Tally marks appear under three small icons: mealworm, curl, beetle. A thin, see-through shed skin glints in the oats.
scenes.narration: Keep the tub at room temperature and out of direct sun. Visit two or three times a week. Look for shed skins. Count and record each stage. Replace the carrot every two or three days.

scenes.tts: The first pupae often appear within a few weeks. A pupa is pale, curled, and still. Use a soft brush to move it to a small dish with a little bran. This keeps the other insects from chewing on it.
scenes.caption: The first pupae often appear within a few weeks. A pupa is pale, curled, and still. Use a soft brush to move it to a small dish with a little bran. This keeps the other insects from chewing on it.
scenes.visual: Use a schematic time lapse. Show the larva shedding its outer skin to reveal a pale, curled pupa with folded legs. Keep the shed skin visible. Show an adult lifting the pupa gently with a soft brush into a separate small dish with a little bran.
scenes.narration: The first pupae often appear within a few weeks. A pupa is pale, curled, and still. Use a soft brush to move it to a small dish with a little bran. This keeps the other insects from chewing on it.

scenes.tts: Picture the pale pupa in its dish. Your child sees it sitting still and wonders what will happen next. What do you think will come out?
scenes.caption: Picture the pale pupa in its dish. Your child sees it sitting still and wonders what will happen next. What do you think will come out?
scenes.visual: The pupa sits alone in the small dish. A high-contrast question card on the left reads: 'What comes out of the pupa?'
scenes.narration: Picture the pale pupa in its dish. Your child sees it sitting still and wonders what will happen next. What do you think will come out?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card and the still pupa. Subtle ambient motion: a slow light shift across the dish and a few oat flakes settling, without revealing the beetle.

scenes.tts: After about one to three weeks as a pupa, a pale beetle comes out. Once it darkens, move it back into the main tub. Check the first guess together. Measure the beetle and compare it with your mealworm measurements.
scenes.caption: After about one to three weeks as a pupa, a pale beetle comes out. Once it darkens, move it back into the main tub. Check the first guess together. Measure the beetle and compare it with your mealworm measurements.
scenes.visual: Show a pale beetle emerging from the pupa and darkening over a schematic time lapse. Use the plastic spoon to move the dark beetle into the main tub. Bring back the “Our guess” notepad and compare the ruler reading with the earlier recorded mealworm lengths.
scenes.narration: After about one to three weeks as a pupa, a pale beetle comes out. Once it darkens, move it back into the main tub. Check the first guess together. Measure the beetle and compare it with your mealworm measurements.

scenes.tts: Look for tiny mealworms in the bedding after a few weeks. Draw the four stages together: egg, larva, pupa, and adult beetle. Ask, 'Which looks like its parent from the start, a kitten or a mealworm?'
scenes.caption: Look for tiny mealworms in the bedding after a few weeks. Draw the four stages together: egg, larva, pupa, and adult beetle. Ask, 'Which looks like its parent from the start, a kitten or a mealworm?'
scenes.visual: A circle forms from four drawings with arrows between them: tiny eggs, a mealworm labeled 'larva', a curled pupa, a dark beetle. Beside the circle, a kitten grows into a cat in one simple step.
scenes.narration: Look for tiny mealworms in the bedding after a few weeks. Draw the four stages together: egg, larva, pupa, and adult beetle. Ask, 'Which looks like its parent from the start, a kitten or a mealworm?'

scenes.tts: Make a plan with your child at the start. Never release the insects outdoors. Offer them to an animal keeper. If nobody takes them, an adult chills them in a sealed container in the fridge for a few hours. Then the adult freezes them in a sealed bag for at least three days before disposal.
scenes.caption: Make a plan with your child at the start. Never release the insects outdoors. Offer them to an animal keeper. If nobody takes them, an adult chills them in a sealed container in the fridge for a few hours. Then the adult freezes them in a sealed bag for at least three days before disposal.
scenes.visual: A drawn garden gate with a crossed-out beetle going through it ('Never release'). Then the tub is handed from one adult hand to another beside a simple chicken drawing.
scenes.narration: Make a plan with your child at the start. Never release the insects outdoors. Offer them to an animal keeper. If nobody takes them, an adult chills them in a sealed container in the fridge for a few hours. Then the adult freezes them in a sealed bag for at least three days before disposal.

scenes.tts: Look back at the drawing and the notes together. Ask, 'What changed before the beetle came out?' Your child can point to what they saw.
scenes.caption: Look back at the drawing and the notes together. Ask, 'What changed before the beetle came out?' Your child can point to what they saw.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the tub on its shelf with the four-stage circle drawing propped beside it. A mealworm and a dark beetle sit side by side on the oats, gently moving.
scenes.narration: Look back at the drawing and the notes together. Ask, 'What changed before the beetle came out?' Your child can point to what they saw.

scenes.line: A mealworm becomes a pupa, then an adult beetle.
scenes.visual: Clean warm end card with a faint four-stage circle in the background. Centered, large, high-contrast text: 'A mealworm becomes a pupa, then an adult beetle.'
